summary: Ellison Banks Findly is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Fred Pfeil. Her academic career includes positions at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, Hartford, where she was an associate professor of religion and Asian studies.

Emanuel Sarkisyanz (1923–2015) was a historian, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tehran and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (c. 1948–1953) before serving as Head at Heidelberg University in 1967.
Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist. She has held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He worked as an editor for the Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1926) and as a Pandit at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library, also holding posts at Sanskrit Pathashala and Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya.

Emi Matsushita is an archaeologist and historian. She studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, later working as a lecturer for the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education and graduate assistant at OSU.

Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. Educated at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (Dr. phil., Lic. theol.), he served there as professor before holding a professorship of Oriental languages at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1860.

Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Berlin, Tübingen, Munich, Göttingen, and Kiel under Albrecht Weber and Franz Kielhorn, he held professorial chairs at Humboldt University of Berlin, Kiel University, and the University of Göttingen.

Emilio Teza (1831–1912) worked in linguistics and Indology, studying under Anton Boller. Following library posts in Venice and Florence, he served as a professor (ordinarius) at the universities of Bologna, Pisa (c. 1861–1886), and Padua (c. 1886–1912).

Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetologist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1993, 1995) and the University of California, Berkeley (2003). Since around 2003, she has held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Emma Georgina Rothschild is a historian who studied at Somerville College and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. She held a professorship at the University of Cambridge from c. 1988 to 2008 and joined Harvard University c. 2008.

Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht Conservatory, Utrecht School of the Arts, and Utrecht University, earning her PhD under Jan Gonda. She served as associate professor of Indian musicology at Utrecht University (1964–1988) and at Amsterdam.

Enamul Haque (1937–2022) was a historian and Indologist educated at the University of Dhaka and the University of Oxford (PhD). He directed the Bangladesh National Museum (1983–1991) and led the International Centre for Study of Bengal Art.

Encho Tamura (1917–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. Educated at Kyushu and Kyoto universities, he served as a professor at Kyushu University (1968–1980) and Kumamoto University, and later directed the Kyushu Historical Museum.

Endo Asai (1927–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as professor at Rissho University (1972–1997) and president of Minobusan University (1998–2002).

Eng Jin Ooi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD in Buddhist Textual Studies at Mahidol University, supervised by Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto, alongside studies under several other academic and traditional teachers.

Enga Teramoto (1872–1940) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He later served as a professor at Otani University from 1915 and as a lecturer at Kyoto University from c. 1923 to 1931.

Enichi Ocho (1906–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa. He worked as a researcher at the Academy of Oriental Culture and later became an emeritus professor at Otani University.

Enryo Inoue (1858–1919) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He founded Toyo University in 1887, where he served as a lecturer and manager.

Ensho Kanakura (1896–1987) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tohoku University (1926–1960) and Rissho University (c. 1958–1978), and served as president of Miyagi University of Education.
Ensho Kobayashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts as professor (attested 1988) and professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Hanazono University.
